title: Turrican II: The Final Fight
build: Triangle disk release from the C64Games archive

records.c: Jump to the music initializer at $6C87. A selects an eight-byte song header at $76FD; this load provides two headers.
Jump to the per-update music driver at $6CEC. This copy updates two SID voices, preserving the third for the resident effect driver.
Jump into the initializer's three-byte fade-state reset. A is stored in $6C13-$6C15; the flight transition passes eight here.
Increment the music stop flag through $6DF2. Later play calls clear all three waveform/control registers while that flag remains set.
Current voice index, saved while helpers temporarily use X. The adjacent byte at $6C0D preserves an effect-record offset during pulse/filter modulation.
Effect-record offset preserved while Y indexes a pulse/filter sequence.
A nonzero value diverts playback to clearing the three SID control registers.
Primary tick countdown, reloaded from the song header's first speed byte.
Secondary tick countdown, reloaded from the second speed byte and controlling the primary tick cadence.
Primary tick reload copied from the selected song header and replaceable by order command $FB.
Secondary tick reload copied from the selected song header and replaceable by order command $FB.
Fade control value, tested by order commands and reset together with the two following fade-state bytes.
Fade countdown reload; when nonzero it enables periodic master-volume decrements.
Active fade countdown, reloaded from $6C14 until master volume reaches zero.
Filter mode bits OR-combined with the current volume when writing $D418.
Master volume, initialized to fifteen and decremented by the enabled fade path.
Three voice-indexed note-duration counters. The playback loop in this load processes voice indices one and zero.
Remaining duration for music voice index one, decremented together with the other two duration slots on the primary tick.
Remaining duration for stored voice index two. Initialization and tick bookkeeping retain this slot, while this load's playback loop emits voices one and zero.
Three note-duration values selected by pattern commands and copied to the active duration counters on notes.
Three update-age counters, reset on a new note and saturated at $FF.

Three offsets for the active instrument records, zero for the rest-duration command.
Three current note numbers, including the saved order-list transposition.
Three transposition addends installed by order-list commands.

Three byte positions in their order streams, including stream loop targets.

Three order-stream high bytes, paired with $6C39.
Three remaining repetitions of the current pattern, installed by order-list commands.
Three waveform/control bytes, sent to the corresponding SID control register.
Three indices into command-driven waveform sequences.
Three indices into the instrument's related pitch sequences.

Three nonzero arpeggio table selectors; zero disables the arpeggio helper.
Three positions within the arpeggio increment streams.
Three generated frequency low bytes sent to the SID voices.
Three generated frequency high bytes.
Three note-age thresholds before target-frequency slides start.
Three frequency-slide magnitudes. Reaching the target clears this field.
Three target note numbers for the frequency-slide helper.
Three byte positions in signed vibrato multiplier streams.
Three low bytes of the computed frequency difference used as the vibrato step.
Three corresponding high bytes for vibrato steps.
Three flags marking whether the current note's vibrato step has been calculated.
Three pulse-width low bytes followed by the shared filter cutoff low byte at $6C72. The modulation helper accepts X three for the filter.
Shared filter cutoff low byte, the fourth entry of the pulse/filter modulation-low array.
Three pulse-width high bytes followed by the shared filter cutoff high byte at $6C76.
Shared filter cutoff high byte, the fourth modulation-high entry.
Four pulse/filter direction states: zero rising, one falling and negative stopped.
Four byte positions in the pulse/filter modulation streams.
Four remaining hold/repeat counts in the pulse/filter streams.
Three flags toggled by pattern command $FA, suppressing pulse initialization and changes.
Global filter-freeze flag toggled by pattern command $F9.

Multiply A by eight and read the selected song header. Set tick speeds, three order pointers and initial note durations; clear order/pattern positions, effect state and stop flags. Set volume fifteen and clear all three SID control registers. Fall through to the fade-state reset.
Store A into the three consecutive fade-state bytes and return. Initialization reaches here with A zero; the separate entry at $6C06 permits a caller-selected value.
Store A into the fade reload at $6C14 and active fade tick at $6C15, then return. Order commands enter here to change or clear the fade without replacing the separate parameter at $6C13.

If stopped, clear all three SID controls. Otherwise clear decimal mode, update fade and tick dividers, then process voices two, one and zero. Expired note durations parse order and pattern streams; other updates apply waveform, pitch, pulse and filter effects. Finish by writing the shared filter cutoff and mode/volume registers.

Save X as the active voice. If its duration is nonzero, update the current instrument effects. Otherwise clear per-note effect state, turn off the existing gate and parse its order stream at the saved position.

Interpret order bytes: $FF reads a byte-position loop target; $80-$BF set transposition; $C0-$DF set the instrument addend; $E0-$FA set pattern repeats. $FB replaces the tick speeds, $FC resets fade and volume, $FD accepts a fade parameter, and $FE reaches the stop entry. A nonnegative byte selects a pattern through $781E/$783C.
Increment the stop flag and return. Subsequent play calls clear all three voice controls through the stop branch.

Select the pattern pointer and saved position. Commands set durations, release overrides, instrument/arpeggio selectors, filter/pulse freeze state or slide parameters. Notes below $60 apply order transposition; bytes $60-$7F select a rest duration. A following $FF ends/repeats the pattern and advances its order position when the repeat count expires.

Convert the selected note to frequency, load its instrument control, attack/decay and sustain/release, initialize pulse width unless frozen, and initialize shared filter parameters unless globally frozen. Write envelope registers and enter the normal SID control/output path.

Apply flagged direct high-frequency increments or the age-derived pitch variation, then target slides or vibrato, waveform/pitch streams, per-voice pulse modulation, shared filter modulation and arpeggio. Gate-timing flags can force early release or noise/reset control before the output registers are written.
Select the voice's seven-register offset and write control, pulse width and frequency. Iterate to the next lower voice index, then write the shared filter cutoff and mode/volume.

Select waveform and pitch sequence pointers from the instrument's waveform mode. $FF reads a sequence loop position, $FE holds, and the pitch sequence's $FD advances then restores the base note frequency. Other pitch entries replace the frequency high byte and clear its low byte.
Operand byte 1 of the LDY instruction at $7139, within the described level routine. This address names an operand inside the instruction, rather than another routine entry.
Follow the selected signed note-offset stream, holding on $80 and jumping to a byte index on $81. Add the current note number and look up its resulting frequency.
Use Y as a note-table index and copy low/high frequency bytes from $73FE/$745E into the active voice's frequency state.

Multiply the slide magnitude by four to form a sixteen-bit frequency step. Add or subtract toward the target note frequency; clamp when it crosses the target, then clear slide/vibrato state and make the target the current note.

On first use compute a frequency difference from an instrument-selected note offset and right-shift it by the selected scale. Later age bounds can adjust that step. Reset to the base note, read the signed multiplier stream and repeatedly add/subtract the step; $81 jumps to a stream index and zero holds the frequency.

Unless frozen for X, clear the modulation stream position and hold count and load its initial direction from bit two of the selected effect record. X zero through two select pulse width; X three selects the shared filter cutoff.

Read an optional modulation stream with loop, hold and repeat commands, or apply the record's constant signed step. Compare against its upper/lower bounds and select stop, reflection or wrap behaviour from the direction flags. Pulse-width and filter cutoff share this implementation through four state slots.
Three SID register offsets for the voice outputs.
Three per-voice filter routing masks combined with the selected filter record.
Twenty-three multiples of eleven converting authored pattern instrument selectors to record offsets.

Reset processor flags/stack and CPU banking, initialize title graphics and interrupts, acknowledge the raster and enter the title foreground wait chain. Input-driven game entry occurs in the raster callback.

Disable interrupts, clear the first forty-seven VIC/SID register locations, copy resident panel/reward/movement tables and restore the level clear pointer. Set the level-load flag, restore processor status and jump through the resident-entry word at $AF53.

Save registers and CPU banking in title scratch, bank normal I/O in and paint eighteen two-colour border strips at paired raster positions. After the last strip install the main raster callback and reset the strip index. Acknowledge the VIC and restore banking/registers.
Jump into the foreground wait chain through $908A. Raster callbacks handle presentation and fire-driven game entry while this chain loops.
Subtract $9A from the rolling XOR key at $0118, recover the decoded byte from the stack and return to the reader's caller. Entered by JMP from $8E08 after its byte/key update.

Draw the lower border's fine-scroll wave, update display controls and route the initial reveal through four presentation phases. In ordinary title mode, fire starts a fade/countdown; its expiry initializes lives/continues and jumps to game setup. In score-entry mode, scan the keyboard instead. Animate six decorative sprites on a divided counter and call the three-voice song driver.
Operand byte 1 of the LDX instruction at $8154, within the described level routine. This address names an operand inside the instruction, rather than another routine entry.
Operand byte 1 of the LDX instruction at $8159, within the described level routine. This address names an operand inside the instruction, rather than another routine entry.

If the score-entry flag is set, call the keyboard scanner. Otherwise poll fire while waiting, start music fade and a countdown on a press, then initialize lives/continues and enter the resident game when it expires. Advance six decorative sprite shapes and wrap their X positions on the presentation divider.

Install the next raster callback and choose lower-panel display settings. During normal title presentation, alternate timed panel changes with a nibble-clearing transition or a two-buffer pixel shift. Copy thirty-two text characters through the transposed glyph lookup for each new font row, update scroll position and restore banking/registers.
